messages.content:
Mira, clattering hooves and surprised yelps break through the afternoon, followed by frantic bleating. A fluffy white sheep with a black face and curled horns bounds toward your group, an ornate scroll held in its mouth.

It waves the scroll toward you as it comes close, the parchment shifting with the movement. The sheep’s approach and the scroll are right in front of you; the startled yelps and bleating continue around them.

The sheep is here with the scroll, but what it wants—and what the scroll contains—is not yet clear. You can address the animal, look over the parchment, or respond to the commotion however you choose. What do you do?
I read the scroll aloud and listen to the sheep.

You read the ornate scroll aloud, its parchment shifting between the sheep’s teeth. As you listen, its frantic bleating changes into cultured Common, spoken with an elven accent and a slight bleat.

“I am Finethir Shinebright,” the sheep says. “A wizard in dire need of aid. I need help recovering a powerful artifact from a dangerous wizard—” He breaks off, his black face turned toward you, the scroll still clamped in his mouth.

The clattering hooves and startled yelps continue around you. Finethir has begun his plea, but hasn’t finished explaining what happened or what he needs. What do you do?
Finethir, tell me where Noke and the wand are, and what guards I should expect.

Finethir turns his black face toward you, the ornate scroll still clamped in his mouth. “Noke has the wand, and he—” He cuts off as approaching howls break into the commotion. The details you asked for—and any warning about guards—don’t come before the interruption.

The sheep’s cultured voice falls silent; the howls draw nearer through the clattering hooves and frantic bleating. What do you do?
I stand between Finethir and the approaching noise, draw my sword, and wait for the pursuers to arrive.

You step between Finethir and the approaching noise, drawing your sword. The half-orc pushes through the crowd with one hand on his greatsword, three large wolves in iron collars leading the way. Behind them, a huge cloaked figure’s heavy footfalls rise above the commotion.

The half-orc fixes his small eyes on the sheep. “That sheep is Master Noke’s... he desires to have it back.” Finethir stays behind you, still clutching the ornate scroll in his mouth. The half-orc and his wolves are close enough to confront; the cloaked figure looms behind them. What do you do?
I lower my sword. Guz, I will not fight you. Finethir can go with you; please let me accompany you to speak to Noke.

You lower your sword. “Guz, I will not fight you. Finethir can go with you; please let me accompany you to speak to Noke.”

The half-orc’s hand remains on his greatsword as he studies you. The three collared wolves crowd close, their presence filling the space between you and Finethir. Behind Guz, the huge cloaked figure’s heavy footfalls continue to rise above the surrounding commotion.

Guz gives no answer yet. His gaze shifts from you to the sheep, the ornate scroll still held in its mouth. “Master Noke desires to have it back,” he repeats. What do you say or do as you wait for his response?
I follow Guz and the wolves at a safe distance, tracking where they take Finethir and looking for the route to Noke.

You try to keep a discreet distance as Guz and the collared wolves move through the crowd, but your attempt to shadow them goes poorly. In the clatter and commotion, you fail to stay unnoticed; the wolves’ iron collars jostle as they press close to Finethir, and Guz’s attention remains fixed on the sheep.

You are still here with Guz, the three wolves, Finethir, and the huge cloaked figure looming behind them. The howling, angry shouts, and occasional screams continue to draw nearer. Guz has said only that Master Noke wants the sheep back; you haven’t learned where he is or what guards await. What do you do?

roll.mechanical_summary: stealth: 2d20kl1+1 = 2 (disadvantage: d20 rolled 1 and 12, kept the lower 1) vs DC 15 -> failure

messages.content: I stop hiding. I hand Finethir over to Guz and stand aside, then openly walk beside them as they leave. I ask Guz to take me to Noke.

You stop hiding and openly offer Finethir to Guz, then fall in beside them as they leave. Guz leads the sheep, the three collared wolves, and the huge cloaked figure away; the crowd’s commotion gradually subsides behind you. His purpose remains the one he stated: to return the sheep to his master, Noke.

But the route carries you only so far. When the noise settles, the white sheep remains close, its ornate scroll within reach, looking from one person to another with unmistakable expectation. Finethir and Guz are gone from sight; you have not yet reached Noke’s home. What do you do with the sheep and its scroll?
I stop hiding and openly follow Guz to Noke’s home. I want to speak to Noke, and I walk along the route they take.

You openly follow the well-trodden track as it leaves the road through a gap in the bushes and winds among tall oaks. Many overlapping prints mark the earth, but you see no one else along the way.

The sparse woodland is quiet and apparently uninhabited. You have not yet reached Noke’s home; the track continues between the trees. What do you do next?
I continue along the well-trodden track through the tall oaks until I reach Noke’s home.

The track continues through sparse woodland without any sign of habitation. Then, through the treetops, a strange compound comes into view: thick platforms woven from living branches span four sturdy oaks, with a flower-filled, bowl-shaped garden raised above the ground and an enclosed wooden-and-branch structure beyond it. Two small huts and a large outhouse stand beneath the platforms.

Three great apes lounge and play with oversized dice on the lawn; iron greatswords lie nearby. From inside the outhouse comes the distinct presence of a brown bear. You have reached the edge of Noke’s compound, but you have not yet approached or entered it. What do you do?
I look around Noke’s home. Describe the buildings, doors, terrain, and visible inhabitants so I can decide how to approach.

You take in the compound from where you stand. Its living-branch platforms span four sturdy oaks: a flower-filled, bowl-shaped garden is raised above the ground, and an enclosed wooden-and-branch structure occupies the central platform beyond it. On the side facing the garden, that structure has a door; evenly spaced, window-sized gaps punctuate its walls. Higher still is a smaller bedroom platform. Root-and-branch slopes connect the levels, while two small huts and a large outhouse sit below.

Three great apes occupy the lawn, lounging and playing with oversized dice. Iron greatswords lie nearby. A brown bear remains inside the outhouse, though you can’t see it from here. No one else is visibly present, and you haven’t approached any of the buildings. How do you want to proceed?
I stay in plain view and call out, "Noke! I have come to talk about Finethir and your wand. Please show yourself." I wait for an answer.

Your call carries through the cluttered central platform. A human wizard works among the ink-spattered papers and intricate beast drawings, with a thin, rune-banded oak wand close at hand.

A voice from within—or from the platform—answers sharply: “Return the sheep!” The space opens into a library and laboratory, a sitting room, and a dining room with a kitchen. The wizard remains amid the worktables; what do you say to him?
I walk to the main door of Noke’s home, knock, and ask to speak with him. I do not attack anyone.

You’re already inside the central platform, among shelves and worktables strewn with ink-spattered papers and intricate beast drawings. The human wizard works amid the clutter, a thin, rune-banded oak wand close at hand.

At your request to speak with him, he answers sharply: “Return the sheep!” The library and laboratory open into a sitting room and a dining room with a kitchen. What do you say to Noke?
